PRESENTATION 
Sh Akash M Ambani 00:00:01 – 00:04:57 (Introduction) 
Like I said, this is the first change as a listed Company. I hope you all are kind to me, but 
welcome to JPL’s Analyst Meeting, and we are very happy to be here. Just before I start, an 
introduction to the team, Mathew is the head of our technology and co-leads, our international 
business expansion with Dan Bailey. He has been part of the Jio leadership team from the 
last 15 years. Anshuman Thakur, I believe most of you all should know him. He is our head 
of strategy and again has been part of the business for the last 12 years. Saurabh Sancheti 
is our CFO, again been part of the business for the last 12 years. Pankaj Pawar is the CEO 
and has been part of the group for over 20 years. Dan Bailey has just joined us and is going 
to co-lead our international business with Mathew Oommen.  
The way I thought we would structure this meeting today is to give you the highlights of what 
we actually saw of the IPO and go into a presentation for Q2, which Pankaj will deliver, and 
then we will open it up to you guys for Q&A. So, obviously, we are extremely ecstatic about 
what has happened over the last week and the entire process that started in the end of 
August. Never thought that this would be the outcome, but some of the numbers that we saw, 
we were raising Rs.30,000 Crores odd and we saw demand of Rs.7.4 lakh crores that is 24.5 
times oversubscription. We saw records across every investor category broken, starting from 
QIB to small HNI, big HNI, retail, and other categories like shareholders and employees. In 
fact, the people who were inside the war room on the last day, the QIB category in the last 
90 seconds, surpassed the previous record, and we had a big celebration at that point of 
time. So, obviously, very, very happy for that, but also for the overall India picture. We have 
known how equity markets have been not only in India but globally too. We had foreign 
investor outflows of close to Rs.48,000 Crores and in a market situation like that for us to 
make a stellar debut makes us very proud and reflects that people were realizing value of 
the business that we have built. Again, they say these overnight successes, I can tell you 
that we have put in extreme hard work over the last 10 years to build this business and we 
will continue to do so. 
What was my personal highlights of it? I think obviously the demand that we had, I think we 
had a fantastic anchor book, an anchor book that has not been seen in India ever before, 
both by the international funds and the domestic funds. Very, very happy to see tech focused 
investors also come in with the likes of Dragoneer and Ninety One and really recognizing us 
as a technology Company. From my point of view, again, it was very heartening to see what 
happened to the rupee also on the second day of our IPO, so that was something that I do 
not think any other IPO has ever caused and from my perspective it was very, very heartening 
to see that. Again, as a Company we are taking the IPO as just a new milestone and we 
move on from here. We believe that the value that we can create over the next decade or so 
is even more than what we have done in our first decade and we will continue to aspire from 
that perspective. To conclude, I just want to say that one of the learnings that I have always 

 
 
3 
taken with me is that never let today’s achievement limit tomorrow’s ambition, and that is 
what we want to carry forward as a Company. So with that, I will hand over to Pankaj to walk 
us through Q2 and then handle the Q&A amongst the team. Thank you very much. 
Sh Pankaj Pawar 00:05:00 – 00:28:28 (Overview) 
Good evening, everyone. I think probably this is the first time when the entire management 
team of JPL is present here. So in a sense, it shows the true commitment to what we have 
been sort of keeping our heads down and trying to deliver over this 10-year period. I think 
today’s objective is just to give the overall perspective on how we look at the business as 
well besides numbers  and the real differentiators vis-a-vis other players in the market. This 
quarter has been an industry leading quarter. Again, 542.4 million customers, 36 million year-
on-year net adds, almost 9 million adds in this quarter itself and then within this the 5G 
customer base has now reached 300 million. So clearly I think if we just look at the Verizon 
and US AT&T, I think this is equal to that size and this has been our clear objective as well, 
keep increasing the base of 5G, and that is happening. 
Broadband homes reaching again an important milestone of 30 million numbers almost 7.3 
million net adds year-on-year and this is one of our main growth engines and I will talk about 
it in a minute. The most important for us always has been what is the engagement and what 
is the usage, now that number is 44.2 GB per month, almost 14% year-on-year growth. ARPU 
has reached now ₹218.8 per month, 3.5% year-on-year growth. 
Revenue from operations ₹40,475 Crores, it is 11.4% year-on-year growth, with that EBITDA 
is ₹.21,879 Crores, 16.6% Y-o-Y growth, 54.1% margin and EBITDA less capex again 
₹15,449 in Q2, which is up 52.5% year-on-year. I think it is heartening to see that as we get 
listed in the first quarter itself, which we are reporting, we are well on our growth path and we 
will explain how we look at, how the trend line will move forward from here.  
I think just to give a perspective, how we just look at the construct of this business, the first 
part is Growth is life, in the Reliance context, but whether it is growth in mobility, whether it 
is in home, it is enterprise where we are in that sense we have a much bigger opportunity to 
chase and the digital services is a major part and of course beyond digital services and 
beyond India’s boundary, whatever Jio wants to do, that is part one. 
The deepen part, deepen is the relationship with the consumers and whatever we do through 
our digital engagements to drive stronger retention, how we want to take it forward.  
The conversion is really the monetization cycle and how do we make sure that finally the 
profit and the cash flows through the operating leverage starts moving in, our cost 
efficiencies, our disciplined capital allocation this is the pillar indicating that.  
And the last part is really where we build our growth engines and whether they are new 
services, new markets, and how do we see this as a real compounding engine going forward. 
I think this is the story I want to narrate in these four buckets in totality.  

 
 
4 
So, first part, is that growth exists in the market and when we were on roadshows this 
question kept coming up again and again is the market plateauing? has the market reached 
its level where there is no scope of growth? and we just want to articulate how we see that 
growth still being there as an opportunity both in terms of volume growth as well as the value 
growth. So, the first part in mobility, we see that today just the 4G and 5G broadband, if you 
look at what the numbers look like, we see that there is still an opportunity of 340 million new 
customers getting added to India’s broadband mobility base of which 240 million is broadly 
of existing 2G base. This 2G customer base exists with the other operators right now and 
they are not addressable by us, but they are paying a good amount of revenue month-on-
month to the other operators, but at the same point in time there is about 100 million base, 
which will get added over the next five years purely because they are reaching the threshold 
age limit and are coming into the new base to the market itself. So, 340 million, which is really 
the size of any large country in the Western markets, that kind of a market we see as an 
opportunity for mobility. 
Now, if you look at currently where we exist, so Jio commands 51% CMS actually in the 
wireless broadband market, but 60% in the 5G subscriber base itself. So clearly, we have 
taken a leading position in this part, and if there is a growth opportunity, we will keep playing 
this game in a consistent way. The home broadband side, the way we look at it is right now, 
just about, if we take 330 million odd homes in India it is about 20% penetration, so almost  
64 million homes are connected. We clearly see that by about FY2031 there is no reason 
why India should not reach almost 46% penetration of Indian homes and if you look at the 
rest of the world it has reached much higher percentages, so there is no reason why India 
should not reach. Probably in 2016, everybody said India does not need mobility broadband 
and even at that stage, Jio said that yes, it is an opportunity. We still believe and we are 
extremely optimistic on this 150 million as a potential opportunity in the fixed broadband 
market, and effectively that is the growth. If we take a look at why Jio is positioned better 
versus anybody else, it is because of the technological advantage, what we feel we have 
versus others and at the run rate currently what we are running in is almost twice that of the 
nearest operator. If you are adding that as a gross base, there is no reason why with the 
proprietary technology deployment we should not keep acquiring at a much faster pace going 
forward. 
The third part, which is really the digital economy part, and as India grows, the way we see 
is there is no reason why India should not reach that $1.4 trillion digital economy and if that 
is about 22% of the gross value-added on the overall economic size actually and if really we 
see that this $1.4 trillion comes in the whole Jio’s model of a digital gateway, and why we call 
it digital gateway. If any digital service provider has to reach to half a billion of Indians, Jio is 
the gateway which exists with them and let me just take a 2-minute break over here just to 
explain the concept of this digital gateway. Most of the  other telcos would say that they are 
just bundling a digital service and offering it actually. While digital gateway as a concept, 
when we look at it, we say that there is a market to be created, and if the market is to be 
created, you do not know how that market will move in. So that means technically you are 
looking at I know the customer behavior, we know the propensity of the customer, which all 
services they would like to consume and if you know that, you are targeting them specifically, 
you are making them aware about the product. By making them aware, you are moving into 

 
 
5 
adoption of a product at the appropriate points in the lifecycle journey. Once that product is 
adopted, you are making them  utilize the product, and that utilization gets converted 
effectively into the monetization cycle. So, it is an awareness to adoption to utilization to 
monetization flywheel and this is easier said than done and when you are trying to particularly 
create a new market for a new service, this becomes quite important. So it is not about just 
bundling a service just for the billing purposes and billing it to the consumer but really pushing 
it further. Some of the examples we will talk about later in the presentation, but it is very 
important that we understand this digital gateway as a concept whether it is for consumers, 
whether it is for homes, whether it is for businesses, is a critical part of what Jio is currently 
pursuing in an overall sense. So, clearly, that was all about really the opportunity which exists 
for Jio in an overall market when India moves towards that digital economy. Clearly, the 
current base in this quarter 542.4 million consumers, 300 million on 5G, but clearly the net 
ads year-on-year 36 million, quarter-on-quarter 9 million, so that line keeps on moving and I 
think it is important that clearly that 300 million outside of China becomes the largest base, 
top two US operators, this is more of that size and it is really important that we keep growing 
this base continuously because that is where the efficiency of Jio’s network keeps coming 
into the place. 
I think it is also important to take a look at when Jio is growing this customer base at a 
particular run rate, what is happening to the overall market at the same point in time in terms 
of the net adds and clearly, I think there is a trend line, which is emerging over there over the 
past one year, and even the numbers which got disclosed by TRAI for the last two days. 5G 
base moving on to that incremental additions quarter-on-quarter 15 million and year-on-year 
66 million. We believe this is the great opportunity for Jio to keep continuing, particularly 
when we do not need any incremental spectrum and when we do not need any incremental 
capex to be deployed, to take our balance 4G base into 5G as well as acquire the base from 
other operators. So clearly from our perspective, 5G is critical. The base moving from 4G to 
5G of Jio itself is important as well as moving in the customers from other networks who feel 
that Jio is offering a better 5G service is also part of that growth line.True 5G as a framework 
and that leading to adoption in the network is going to be the theme as we move forward. 
Fixed wireless access will also be one of the main driver for our home business and by now 
you know that Jio looks at a customer base not as a service actually. We are not saying you 
are a mobility customer, you are a home customer, you are a one-line customer or you are a 
two-line customer, ultimately we are looking at them as a customer unit. So effectively you 
may be using my one service or two service or three services and actually we finally want to 
know how much is that Jio can expect from you, whether from the connectivity services or 
incrementally from the digital services also. So clearly home is an important element of our 
overall strategy. We have reached the 30 million mark, almost half of that coming from fixed 
wireless access actually. This is 2x of the nearest competitor, Jio continues to be the largest 
FWA operator anywhere in the world and of course, the UBR, by now we all know exactly 
how Jio is deploying that and effectively, that becomes the core technology as we move 
forward, of course whatever the fiber we are deploying that we use, but certainly I think the 
elements of the UBR evolution, the way the technology has evolved and whatever work we 
have done that allows us to eliminate a lot of negativities, which people feel about that 

 
 
6 
technology and that is why we feel more confident about using UBR as a primary source of 
our growth engine for the purpose of home broadband. 
This is where I want to again take a little bit of time to explain the philosophy because I think 
now it is important that if our journey is going to move forward from here how we move our 
flywheel section. The first flywheel is the way our technology element operates actually, and 
this is where Jio’s technology edge comes into the play. Many of those things go under 
appreciated, but we are saying that if there are unique capabilities within the Jio architecture, 
those we can leverage much better than other telco operators, that allows us to actually play 
and offer better services in a differential way to the consumers, that allows us to, of course, 
not just attract the new customers but include the monetization as well and that allows us to 
make sure that we can keep reinvesting in the newer capabilities in the network and there 
are many examples of this. One of the examples which you saw in our recent AGM was how 
we embed the AI capabilities into our voice calls itself and I think these are some of the 
capabilities which are unique because of the core network we have deployed, the way the 
network has been deployed within Jio’s architecture and there is a series of such capabilities, 
which will allow us to keep offering the services in a better way. 
The second part is when you offer this service and customer is using 44.2 GB, and actually 
you are using the data insights  in a meaningful way. Of course, the data is anonymized, but 
having said that, if you are able to use that data more meaningfully to deliver more meaningful 
personalized services, that is where the adoption of service starts happening and that is why 
the data flywheel starts operating over there and again that allows us to offer relevant 
services that allow us to monetize the services in a better way.  
The third part is really if you are doing this, how do you do the distribution in a better way and 
distribution is not only about physical distribution, the way the physical and the digital part 
kicks in, and how you create those markets.  
So, if you are moving these three flywheels in a systematic way that is where you are saying 
that we are not dependent on one line item for increasing the revenue. This is where the line 
items of how you use this machine to get more revenue per customer starts coming into the 
play and that is the way Jio operates in. Now, when we do that, what are the sort of evidences 
of doing that in a differential way? Gemini was one of the first examples and you see some 
of the other brands mentioned over here in the slide. This is a select list of names within 
productivity, performance, media, and even in financial services, but really, there is a long 
list which is behind this actually. So virtually, if there is a product that needs to be pushed in 
and that product is going to create value for the consumer that is where the wallet share of 
the consumer I can get. If I am able to give something to the consumers where I can get that 
wallet share, that money comes to us and that it is more valuable because rather than just 
saying that I will keep charging you in one particular for connectivity, here you are giving 
more value to the customer, and you are getting more wallet share back. I think it does not 
get restricted only to digital services it goes beyond digital services also. So, some of the 
financial services, what you look at, this is like saying, can I create a market, which is a 
systematic investment plan market, in the markets where it never existed? There are first 
time to SIP individuals. Will you get them to do an invest in a SIP? That is extremely valuable. 

 
 
7 
If you are selling a wealth management plan why a wealth management plan cannot be taken 
by somebody who is a first-time job person, and if you make him invest that, that whole logic 
changes, actually. So, really, what Jio is moving towards is that the connectivity is an enabler, 
but keep on bringing on the top of that an ecosystem of 1P services, that is the services 
which we have brought, but the 3P services which come from the ecosystem partners and if 
both of these play together you are creating value. In most of these cases, there are sort of 
three tenets. The first tenet is the cost of creating this belongs to the other partner, so if I am 
creating Gemini as an ecosystem, Gemini’s cost of offering service did not come to us. That 
cost was borne by the partner actually. Second tenet is when you do this, you are actually 
playing the role of how you are creating India as a market and again, in the Gemini context, 
it was not about just saying that how many million customers you offered the service, but it 
was about if AI is to be used by young consumers is it a voice AI? If it is a voice AI can we 
drive it in not just 12 languages, but you can go into language variants like Tulu and Magadhi 
and all kinds of Brijwasi language? Can you drive that consumption from two minutes to 
seven minutes? Right now it has gone beyond seven minutes actually. So you are actually 
looking at how the consumption can happen, which finally results into the monetization. This 
is where Jio plays a role. It is not just limited to that I had done a joint billing and achieved 
everything. Third tenet is the cost, there is a way of creating a product and till you are saying 
it is not only the acquisition of a consumer. A distributor typically would say that you pay me 
for distributing your product, but in this case, you are co-creating a market. When you co-
create a market, there is a revenue stream, which flows to you over a lifecycle of the 
consumer. So whenever the consumer starts getting monetized, the money keeps coming to 
you. So that is the logic of this whole digital gateway concept. I think it takes time for people 
to figure out how that works but as we move along that each line item keeps creating value 
addition to Jio’s revenue stream. This does not work only on mobility or home and I am just 
giving an example of how this plays on in the mobility and how it goes on into the home as 
well. In mobility the basic mobility SA network makes sure that the services get offered in an 
appropriate way, whether you do the slice, whether you do the unique way of embedding 
certain things in the core network, everything, but beyond that are the digital service 
capabilities that are getting added. Now, one may say that I am just bundling it. That is not 
this play and I want to make a difference between a pure bundled product versus where we 
can create a market and there is a difference in the revenue stream coming from both the 
things. I think when you need to do this, you need to give the basic underlying product 
properly and create the value for the consumer. That means the service experience needs 
to be precise. Then only your consumption will increase and that converts into GB and that 
is why you see GB per consumer continuously going up in Jio’s case.  
How do you do this at home actually, and home is a critical piece because once in a home 
you exist it is literally like you are becoming an OS for the home and it is connectivity to the 
home is not just the last point, connectivity or getting a customer connect is the point number 
one, but what you are doing is you are layering a whole lot of services on the top of that. 
Everybody will say basic internet is a must or TV is a must. Let us take that as a given. What 
you keep adding on top of that, this is where the compute comes in, this is where the cloud 
gaming comes in. Compute as a hardware in India does not exist, and Jio is giving that for 
Rs.400, Rs.500 per month. Imagine that somebody is paying Rs.600, Rs.700 as a baseline 
product and paying that Rs.400 on top of that, just because your data security gets taken 

 
 
8 
care, compute gets taken care. You put a gaming terminal on top of that. You do not need to 
buy a full console or you do not need to buy the subscription to the gaming titles. You get 
Rs.300 for that. You put on top of that video analytics. Your set-top box starts acting as an 
AI gateway into the home. So it is a whole series of digital services you are layering on the 
top of that, that is the way the digital gateway model gets manifested, whether it is in the 
hand or at the home.  
The same way it gets manifested in the enterprises as well. The way we look at it, is a three-
tiered market - large enterprises, medium enterprises, small enterprises and really, those 
small merchants., The market is almost 80 million small merchants out there who do not have 
any CIO, who do not have any ability to get those services in and when you look at that, the 
connectivity is the first part, but the cloud and compute the platforms and security are next. 
So you are not offering the services just as vertical line items and saying I am giving this to 
you, you take it. But you are saying, I will offer that full framework to you and you may be a 
bank branch, or you may be a pharmacy store. This is an area where we believe the real 
opportunity of digital services starts coming in. This is where our highest growth opportunity 
is, and this is what we are focusing on.  
From all these three things, the way we start rolling it up, it adds into the connectivity revenue 
and effectively that is the digital services play. Now may be Saurabh will talk about the 
financials.  
Sh Saurabh Sancheti 00:28:32 – 00:34:02 (Financials) 
Thank you. So basically, how do we operate? We have Growth, which is about getting more 
users in or acquiring more users, Deepen, which means engage them more, and give them 
more services. Going to Convert which is about the whole monetization flowing into the 
overall revenue and EBITDA and cash flows and finally Build, use this cashflow to build on 
further the three flywheels Pankaj was talking about. The first part which is grow, 9.1 million 
user additions for the quarter, industry beating numbers, taking the total base to 542.4 million 
users and like Pankaj said we added 66 million 5G users, 36 million overall net adds, growing 
very strong and we have plenty of room here for growth. 340 million new users to come to 
4G and 5G and more importantly like we have always maintained a 50% plus market share, 
so I think the volume growth is there. The second part which is Deepen is on engagement 
and the best measure of engagement and the best measure of even quality of customer is 
the number of GBs a consumer consumes because that means the consumer was totally 
attached to the network. 44.2 GB per user per month that is the kind of metric. See how it 
has moved consistently every quarter since the last one year from 38.7 GB per user per 
month. The second metric, which is ARPU, which all of you are fascinated about, is ₹211.4 
going to ₹218.8. So, ₹7 purely on a better subscriber mix. But one thing which is very 
important here is this is just the connectivity business and the connectivity revenue. The 
digital part of the monetization does not sit here. So, where does it sit? Which is the second 
part of the metric, if you go to financial KPI, standalone JPL up 23% year-on-year to ₹4,881 
Crores. And this is also part of the convert. If you look at the consol, 11.4% revenue growth 
going to ₹40,475 crores of revenue. And EBITDA, growing faster, 16.6% year-on-year growth 
to ₹21,879 Crores. And just look at the operating leverage playing out, the overall 250 basis 

 
 
9 
point Y-o-Y expansion in margins. So, almost 78% of all incremental revenues are flowing 
through to EBITDA during the quarter. Of course, all of this flows through to EBIT, PBT and 
finally PAT as well. PAT growing 13.7% year-on-year to ₹8,387 crores and this is substantial 
because now all of the 5G assets is capitalized so the costs are flowing through to P&L. On 
cashflows, EBITDA less cash capex which is what we keep focus on, for the H1 it is at 
₹32,130 crores and for this quarter itself it is Rs.15,449 Crores. That has led to our net 
leverage going down to 0.11x as of 30th September. With the IPO proceeds, we are net debt 
positive. I think one more important metric, in one quarter itself we have seen a 80 basis point 
improvement in return on capital employed to now 11%. So, what is the debt looking like in 
the balance sheet, almost ₹59,000 crores of borrowings. All of these are, of course, 30th 
September number. You can add ₹30,188 crores of issue proceeds to this to know the actual 
cash position and plus the business cash flows also. ₹50,000 crores of marketable cash and 
marketable securities means a net debt on 30th September, was ₹8,822 crores and a 
leverage of 0.1 times. So, very healthy set of metrics across. Like I said, you have Grow, 
acquire more users, Deepen, which means higher engagement, and you get more services 
per user, the whole digital gateway, which Pankaj spoke about. The Convert, the financial 
set of numbers are already there for you to see, and the growth there. And finally, for the 
Build part, also we have a few slides on which we will talk about. If you talk about the 
connectivity entity ₹35,307 crores of revenue for the quarter, up 10.8% year-on-year. EBITDA 
growing faster, the operating leverage is playing here, 14.7% Y-o-Y to ₹20,505 crores, and 
margin now touching 58.1%. 
So, just summarizing the consolidated numbers, I have spoken about these numbers 11.4% 
Y-o-Y growth, revenue growing to ₹40,475 crores, 16.6% EBITDA growth growing to ₹21,879 
crores, and of course the EBITDA margins at 54.1%, 250 basis point improvement Y-o-Y and 
profit after tax also healthy at ₹.8,387 crores, 13.7% Y-o-Y growth. On the build part, there 
are some exciting things, but I would invite Mr. Akash to just brief us. 
Sh Akash M Ambani 00:34:08 – 00:37:37 (Summary) 
Thank you. So, really, what I want to summarize is the pillars of our future growth. And I think 
we spent a lot of time speaking about how we operate very differently than a telco. The basis 
of that is our proprietary technology. Today, we have all our integrated 4G, 5G stack covering 
all our customers. We built our UBR. You have seen that now fixed wireless is 50% of our 
entire fixed broadband base. New additions are also being majorly led by our fixed wireless 
base. Pankaj explained in detail the concept of a digital gateway and how that is very, very 
different from a bundling offer. The word that I would use is, especially regarding the Gemini 
one, is a new market creation rather than really saying that these are benefits that were 
passed on to users. And that is why we are seeing the numbers that we have with Gemini. 
Again, enterprise is something that we think is a major growth opportunity. The bottom line 
here is that India has 350,000 lease lines and, it accounts to maybe 5% of the total ICT 
spend. So what we want to double down here and do is to ensure that our digital solutions 
are the ones that help us churn those users to us and of course, the small medium businesses
